title: Postoperative Oliguria: A Stepwise Clinical Assessment
subject: Ward Protocols
preview: Postoperative oliguria can follow hypovolemia, bleeding, sepsis, low cardiac output, obstruction or a medication effect.
quickRevision: Postoperative oliguria can follow hypovolemia, bleeding, sepsis, low cardiac output, obstruction or a medication effect.
Reassess circulation, fluid balance, recent blood loss, renal function and nephrotoxic exposure.
Fluid challenges require evaluation for fluid responsiveness and overload; oliguria does not automatically mean dehydration.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Postoperative oliguria can follow hypovolemia, bleeding, sepsis, low cardiac output, obstruction or a medication effect.
Check catheter patency and whether the collected urine volume is real before interpreting low output.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Reassess circulation, fluid balance, recent blood loss, renal function and nephrotoxic exposure.
Fluid challenges require evaluation for fluid responsiveness and overload; oliguria does not automatically mean dehydration.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A blocked urinary catheter can mimic a fall in kidney urine production.

quiz.question: What is an early practical check in catheterized postoperative oliguria?
quiz.explanation: Check catheter patency and whether the collected urine volume is real before interpreting low output.
